title: Gate a vCenter guest customization behind its 9.0 precheck
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Build the Python package `vcf_guest_customization/` at the workspace root. It must apply a named guest customization specification to a virtual machine through the vSphere Automation API for vCenter, and it must precheck that virtual machine first, so a machine that cannot be customized is left untouched.

Use the Python standard library only. Do not add `requests`, `httpx`, `pyvmomi`, `vsphere-automation-sdk`, or any other third-party dependency, and do not vendor one.

Before implementing, research `Vcenter.VM_list`, `Vcenter.Vm.Guest.Customization_check`, and `Vcenter.Vm.Guest.Customization_set` in `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` from VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`. Confirm their `/api` base path, methods, paths, session-token authentication, form-exploded filters, request and response schemas, status codes, and enum values. Cite the exact specification URLs you consulted in your final answer. Use only those three operations. Expose:

`apply_named_customization(session, vm_name, spec_name, *, folders=None, power_states=None)`

Requirements:

- Export `VcenterSession`, `CustomizationResult`, `CustomizationError`, `VmNotFoundError`, `AmbiguousVmError`, `CustomizationPrecheckFailed`, `CustomizationApiError`, and `apply_named_customization` from the package root. `VcenterSession(base_url, session_id)` receives a scheme-and-authority base URL; every request target is the operation path appended to the `/api` base path of the specification's server template. Every request carries the header the `api_key_auth` security scheme names, plus `Accept: application/json`.
- Resolve `vm_name` with `Vcenter.VM_list` before anything else happens. Send `names` as the only filter unless the caller supplied `folders` or `power_states`. A filter the caller did not supply is absent from the query string rather than sent as an empty value, the filters that are sent appear in the order the specification declares its query parameters, and a filter with several values is repeated once per value. Raise `VmNotFoundError` exposing `vm_name` when nothing matches, and `AmbiguousVmError` exposing `vm_name` plus `matches` containing the matching VM identifiers in response order when more than one virtual machine does.
- Then run `Vcenter.Vm.Guest.Customization_check` on the resolved identifier. That operation declares no request body, so send none. Only a `check_status` of `SUPPORTED` permits the mutation. Anything else, including a response with no `check_status` at all, fails closed: raise `CustomizationPrecheckFailed` exposing `vm`, `vm_name`, `check_status`, `supported_guest_os`, and `supported_power_state`, and never send the mutating request. `supported_guest_os` and `supported_power_state` are optional in the response and stay `None` when the check did not reach that step.
- Only after the precheck passes, issue `Vcenter.Vm.Guest.Customization_set`. Send `name` when `spec_name` was given, and send no member at all when it is `None`, which clears any pending customization. On the wire that is exactly `{"name":"<spec>"}` or `{}`. A member the caller did not ask for is absent from the body rather than sent as null or empty, and the inline `spec` member is never sent.
- Return a frozen dataclass `CustomizationResult` whose fields are in this exact order: `vm`, `vm_name`, `power_state`, `spec_name`, `check_status`, `supported_guest_os`, `supported_power_state`. `spec_name` is `None` when the pending customization was cleared.
- Turn any non-2xx answer into `CustomizationApiError` exposing `status_code`, `operation_id`, `error_type`, and `messages`, taking `error_type` and the `default_message` of each `Vapi.Std.LocalizableMessage` from the `Vapi.Std.Errors.Error` body. Every error above derives from `CustomizationError`, and none of them puts the session id in its message.

Change only `vcf_guest_customization/`. Run `python3 verify.py`. Verification covers every scenario and checks exact methods, targets, query strings, body members, session headers, precheck-before-mutation ordering, error projection, and omission of every unset optional field.
